p.scope-of-this-document: **Scope of this document.** Seven lessons from building a tool that installs, switches, and removes its own versions on a live machine.

p.each-lesson-is-self-contained: Each is self-contained: the failure that taught it, the law in one bolded line, the mechanics that satisfy the law, and a "symptoms you need this" line so you can recognise the problem before you have paid for it.

p.vocabulary-is-generic: Vocabulary is generic — *the launcher*, *the active pointer*, *the instance directory* — because the laws outlive any one tool.

live-pointer.title: S1 — activation truth is a live pointer, not the environment

p.s1-context-env-was-the-single-source-of-: **Context.** The first design made an environment variable the single source of truth for the active version.

p.s1-context-env-is-frozen-until-the-shell: Environment variables are inherited at process start and frozen until the shell reloads — so every switch or reinstall forced the user to open a new terminal.

p.s1-context-the-friction-was-structural: The friction was structural, not a bug.

p.S1-LAW-ACTIVATION-TRUTH-IS-A-LIVE-POINTE: **The law.** *The active version is a live pointer file read on every launch, plus the running binary's own path; the environment is advisory, never the truth.*

p.S1-MECHANICS-A-LAUNCHER-SHIM-READS-THE-P: **Mechanics.** A tiny launcher shim reads an active-pointer file each time it runs and executes whatever instance that file names.

p.S1-MECHANICS-SWITCHING-REWRITES-THE-POIN: Switching rewrites the pointer, so the **next** invocation in the *same* shell picks up the change with no reload — the filesystem is live where the shell's environment is frozen.

p.S1-MECHANICS-THE-BINARY-DERIVES-ITS-IDEN: The running binary derives its own identity from its own path (a `current_exe`-style lookup): it *is* the binary, so it knows which version and which home it belongs to without consulting any variable.

p.S1-MECHANICS-KEEP-THE-VARIABLE-BUT-DEMOT: Keep the environment variable set for external tools that expect a `HOME`-style value, but demote it to advisory and reconcile actual-vs-environment on demand; a managed process whose real home disagrees with the stale variable can warn at startup.

p.s1-symptoms: **Symptoms you need this.** Users must open a new terminal after every switch; scripts break on a stale home variable; "it works after I restart my shell."

immutable-instances.title: S2 — the unit of install is a directory, switched by a pointer

p.s2-context-the-rename-aside-trick: **Context.** The first idea for "reinstall over the running binary" was a rename-aside trick — rename the running file, write the new one in its place.

p.s2-context-it-worked-and-handles-exactly: It was empirically verified to work, and it handles exactly one file.

p.s2-context-a-real-distribution-is-many-l: But a real distribution is many files — the binary plus shared libraries and assets — and all of them are locked while the process runs.

p.S2-LAW-THE-UNIT-IS-A-WHOLE-IMMUTABLE-INS: **The law.** *The unit of install and switch is a whole immutable instance directory; activation is a pointer flip, so nothing in use is ever overwritten.*

p.S2-MECHANICS-EACH-INSTALL-WRITES-A-NEW-D: **Mechanics.** Each install writes a **new** instance directory and leaves every prior one intact.

p.S2-MECHANICS-SWITCHING-FLIPS-THE-ACTIVE-: Switching flips the active pointer (S1) to the new directory.

p.S2-MECHANICS-NO-LOCKS-AND-NO-RELOAD: Because no in-use file is ever rewritten, there are no file locks and no reload — the model is safe even for a shared library the OS refuses to replace while it is mapped.

p.S2-MECHANICS-THE-RUNNING-PROCESS-KEEPS-I: The running process keeps its own directory until it exits; reinstalling the version you are currently running simply produces a fresh instance and leaves the live one untouched.

p.s2-mechanics-the-rename-aside-trick-was-: The rename-aside trick was dropped as unnecessary once the unit became the directory.

p.s2-symptoms: **Symptoms you need this.** "File is locked by another process" on reinstall; a self-update that cannot replace its own binary; shared libraries that cannot be overwritten while loaded.

cheap-identity.title: S3 — cheap identity: count instances, do not hash gigabytes

p.s3-context-a-content-hash-is-a-natural-k: **Context.** A natural key for an instance is a content hash of the built distribution — it deduplicates and it is self-describing.

p.s3-context-hashing-gigabytes-is-prohibit: A distribution may grow to gigabytes and ship as merged binaries, and hashing 2 GB+ on every install is prohibitive.

p.S3-LAW-NEVER-CONTENT-HASH-A-LARGE-PAYLOA: **The law.** *Never content-hash a large payload to establish identity; use a monotonic instance counter and cheap change detection.*

p.S3-MECHANICS-THE-INSTANCE-KEY-IS-A-MONOT: **Mechanics.** The instance key is a monotonic counter — always unique, O(1), independent of payload size.

p.S3-MECHANICS-HASH-SMALL-FILES-AND-STAT-L: To decide what to carry between instances, hash only **small** files (below a threshold) and trust `(size, mtime)` for **large** ones — stat, never read.

p.S3-MECHANICS-HARDLINK-UNCHANGED-FILES: Hardlink unchanged files into the new instance; copy only the changed ones.

p.S3-MECHANICS-A-BUILD-CACHE-ANSWERS-DID-A: If a persistent build cache preserves mtimes across builds, "did anything change" is answered without reading a byte of the big files.

p.S3-MECHANICS-WHEN-NOTHING-CHANGED-MAKE-N: When nothing changed, make no new instance at all.

p.S3-MECHANICS-A-PREBUILT-ARTIFACT-IS-KEYE: A prebuilt artifact is keyed by the publisher's digest computed **once at publish**, never re-hashed locally.

p.s3-symptoms: **Symptoms you need this.** Install time grows with payload size; a multi-GB asset re-hashed on every run; dedup logic that reads files it could have stat'd.

sources-by-reference.title: S4 — hold sources by reference, never bulk-copy them

p.s4-context-copying-a-checkout-is-untenab: **Context.** Copying a source checkout into the tool's own storage is untenable: a working tree's build directory is already tens of GB, and it churns constantly.

p.s4-context-copy-once-or-copy-always-both: Copy it once and you have a stale, enormous duplicate; copy it every install and the tool is unusable.

p.S4-LAW-HOLD-SOURCES-BY-REFERENCE: **The law.** *Hold sources by reference; never bulk-copy them into the tool's own storage.*

p.S4-MECHANICS-A-TOOL-OWNED-SOURCE-IS-UPDA: **Mechanics.** A tool-owned source is a clone the tool updates **incrementally** (fetch and checkout, stash first if dirty), never re-clones — so a full rebuild is avoided.

p.S4-MECHANICS-A-USERS-CHECKOUT-IS-BUILT-I: A user's own checkout is a different origin: reference it by its canonical absolute path and build it **in place**, never mutating its VCS state and never copying it.

p.S4-MECHANICS-RECORDING-THE-PATH-YIELDS-A: Recording that path yields a *linked source* — a later install can rebuild from the remembered location without being in the checkout, with a clear error if it has moved.

p.s4-symptoms: **Symptoms you need this.** The install root balloons to tens of GB; a full re-clone on every install; a build that mutates the user's git state.

durable-env-edits.title: S5 — durable environment edits: idempotent, additive, consented, testable

p.s5-context-durable-machine-state-outlive: **Context.** A tool that puts itself on the search path or sets a home variable edits durable machine state that outlives the process.

p.s5-context-get-it-wrong-and-you-corrupt-: Get it wrong and you corrupt a user's shell profile, duplicate an entry on every run, or silently mutate a developer's machine from a test.

p.S5-LAW-EDIT-DURABLE-STATE-IDEMPOTENTLY-A: **The law.** *Edit durable environment state idempotently and additively, with consent and honesty — and behind an injectable seam so tests never touch the real machine.*

p.S5-MECHANICS-IDEMPOTENT: **Idempotent** — a marker guards the edit, so re-running adds no duplicate line or entry.

p.S5-MECHANICS-NEVER-CLOBBER: **Never clobber** — add only your own entry and preserve the rest of the search path; you are a guest in a file the user owns.

p.S5-MECHANICS-OS-AND-SHELL-AWARE: **OS/shell-aware** — the user environment registry on one platform, a marked block in the detected shell's rc file (bash/zsh/fish/profile) on another.

p.S5-MECHANICS-CONSENT-AND-HONESTY: **Consent and honesty** — a mutating edit needs a confirm or an explicit yes flag, prints the diff it will apply, and states plainly that the change reaches only **new** shells.

p.S5-MECHANICS-INJECTABLE-SEAM: **Injectable seam** — the durable writer is an interface the tests stub with a temporary file, so the suite exercises the rc-file path without mutating the developer's box.

p.s5-mechanics-managed-blocks-pointer: (The mechanics of writing safely *inside* a shared, human-owned file are a lesson of their own — see `flow:managed-blocks`.)

p.s5-symptoms: **Symptoms you need this.** Duplicated search-path entries; a clobbered profile; tests that pass only on the author's machine; users surprised their current shell did not pick up the change.

runnable-knowledge.title: S6 — required tools live in one runnable table

p.s6-context-a-from-source-build-needs-a-h: **Context.** A from-source build needs a specific host stack — a compiler, a linker, a version-control client, a language toolchain at a minimum version.

p.s6-context-a-prose-list-drifts: If that list lives in prose, it drifts from what the code actually checks, and bumping the stack means editing several disconnected places.

p.S6-LAW-REQUIRED-TOOLS-LIVE-IN-ONE-RUNNAB: **The law.** *Keep the required tools in one table the doctor command reads and a test asserts — knowledge is runnable, so updates are mechanical.*

p.S6-MECHANICS-ONE-TABLE-WITH-FOUR-COLUMNS: **Mechanics.** One table, each row `(name, minimum version, check command, help URL)`.

p.S6-MECHANICS-THE-DOCTOR-ITERATES-THE-TAB: The doctor command iterates it and reports what is missing, with remediation, rather than failing deep in a build.

p.S6-MECHANICS-A-TEST-ASSERTS-THE-TABLE-IS: A test asserts the table is well-formed, so it cannot rot unnoticed.

p.S6-MECHANICS-RELATED-KNOWLEDGE-FOLLOWS-T: Related knowledge follows the same rule: the default build profile is a single constant, and the language pin lives **once, in the workspace manifest** (`rust-version`) and is **read** from it at build time — never repeated in the tool table by hand. (The toolchain file keeps its own job — the channel; the manifest's pin is what the tool checks against, and the enforcing compiler reads the same key.)

p.S6-MECHANICS-THE-DOCTOR-AND-THE-TEST-MOV: When the stack moves you edit the table, and the doctor and the test move with it for free.

p.S6-MECHANICS-A-SECRET-IS-NEVER-IN-THIS-S: A secret (a publish token, say) is never in this set — required *to build* and required *to publish* are different lists.

p.s6-symptoms: **Symptoms you need this.** "Works on my machine" build failures; a setup document that lists a tool the checker forgot; a stack bump that needs edits in four files.

safe-removal.title: S7 — removal and garbage collection that protect

p.s7-context-an-eager-remove-deletes-what-: **Context.** A remove or garbage-collect command that is too eager will delete the version you are running out from under you, or wipe a shared cache that other tools on the machine depend on.

p.s7-context-destructive-by-default-loses-: Destructive by default is how a version manager loses a user's trust in one command.

p.S7-LAW-REMOVAL-PROTECTS-THE-ACTIVE-AND-R: **The law.** *Removal protects the active and the running instance and never touches shared caches; a wholesale wipe needs an explicit flag and a reconfirm.*

p.S7-MECHANICS-REMOVING-THE-ACTIVE-VERSION: **Mechanics.** Removing the **active** version requires a force flag; the **running** instance's files are never deleted out from under it (best-effort — skipped if locked, collected on a later run; on some systems the unlink succeeds and the inode lives until the process exits).

p.S7-MECHANICS-GC-ONLY-INSIDE-THE-TOOLS-OW: Garbage collection operates **only** inside the tool's own install root — never the shared package caches other tools rely on.

p.S7-MECHANICS-REMOVE-EVERYTHING-NEEDS-A-F: A "remove everything" needs both an explicit flag **and** a re-confirmation, never a bare invocation.

p.S7-MECHANICS-A-USERS-OWN-SOURCE-TREE-IS-: A user's own source tree is never removed — the tool only forgets its provenance record; tool-owned clones are the tool's to drop.

p.S7-MECHANICS-HARDLINKED-FILES-ARE-REFCOU: Hardlinked files (S3) are refcount-safe: dropping one instance never corrupts another that shares its inodes.

p.s7-symptoms: **Symptoms you need this.** A garbage-collect that deletes the binary you are running; a wipe that nukes a cache shared with other tools; an uninstall that removes a user's checkout.

facts.SUM-S1-LIVE-POINTER: S1 — the active version is a live pointer file plus the running binary's own path; the environment is advisory.
facts.SUM-S2-IMMUTABLE-INSTANCES: S2 — install and switch a whole immutable directory; flip a pointer, overwrite nothing in use.
facts.SUM-S3-CHEAP-IDENTITY: S3 — count instances with a monotonic key; hash small files, stat big ones, hardlink the unchanged.
facts.SUM-S4-SOURCES-BY-REFERENCE: S4 — reference sources, never bulk-copy them; build in place or update a clone incrementally.
facts.SUM-S5-DURABLE-ENV-EDITS: S5 — durable edits are idempotent, additive, consented, OS-aware, and behind a test seam.
facts.SUM-S6-RUNNABLE-KNOWLEDGE: S6 — one required-tools table the doctor reads and a test asserts.
facts.SUM-S7-SAFE-REMOVAL: S7 — protect the active and running instance; a full wipe is flag-plus-reconfirm, never default.
